utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everyone. Madam Registrar, can you call -- or Mr. Registrar, it is, can you call the case, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good afternoon, Your Honour, good afternoon, everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-99-36-I, the Prosecutor versus Stojan Zupljanin. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: And may I have the appearances, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is Anna Richterova, and I'm assisted today by trial attorney Karen Beausey and Crispian Smith, our case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: And for the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm Tomislav Visnjic and I'm the duty Defence attorney in this case. I would just like to draw your attention that it seems that the B/C/S translation, we are not hearing it on channel 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Oh, that was my next point here, that I want to make it -- to be sure, to feel confident, that everyone is following the proceedings in a language they understand. The accused, you're not following the proceedings in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I'm receiving the translation now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you. If at any time during this hearing there is any problem, please let me know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not getting the Serbian translation on my monitor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Can someone see to that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: For the accused's information, there is no transcript in B/C/S. It's only in English but you receive interpretation through your headphones. So we will proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the accused, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: I did not receive interpretation of what the accused said now. We may proceed? Yes. Mr. Zupljanin, you understand that you have duty counsel representing you here today for the purpose of this initial appearance. We will come to the question of counsel and representation later on, but do you have any comments to this, that he is assisting you today for the purpose of this initial appearance?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have nothing particular to say, and I'm really happy with Mr. Visnjic representing me at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you. Before we proceed and go to the substance of this initial appearance, it is my duty to inform you that you have the right to remain silent. This is a right you enjoy under the rules of evidence and procedure and basically it means that no one can force to you say anything, to answer any questions, and this applies at all times, from the beginning of the proceedings until they are brought to an end. This right to remain silent arises out of a broader right that you have against self-incrimination, to not be compelled to testify against yourself or to confess guilt. Is that clear?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is clear. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you. By the order of the president of this Tribunal dated 11 June 2008, this case was assigned to Trial Chamber II. In an order dated 23 June 2008, Judge Kwon, as the Presiding Judge of the Trial Chamber in this case has designated me as the Pre-Trial Judge and by another order of the same day, as the judge for the purposes of this hearing, this initial appearance. I will now proceed to give some basic information about the indictment. Stojan Zupljanin is the only accused in this indictment, with case number IT-99-36-I. This indictment was confirmed by Judge Rodrigues on 17 December 1999 and made public on 13 July 2001. This indictment has later been amended and the second amended indictment was filed on 6 October 2004 and is the operative indictment in the present case. I have been informed, through the Senior Legal Officer, that there may be a mistake in the indictment. If the Prosecutor wants to briefly touch on that now perhaps?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That's correct. We identified a small typo when the date of birth was typed as 28 instead of 22nd, and we submitted also the birth certificate of Mr. Zupljanin, which is confirming the fact that the right date of birth should be 22nd of September.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you. And this will, I guess, in due course, then, be amended.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: That's correct. It is our intention to file a new amended indictment and, of course, this error will be fixed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you for that. I will now proceed with a summary of the indictment, and this I do also for the benefit of the public following these proceedings. I will start with a few words of what kind of crimes you are charged with. The accused is charged with the following counts as set forth in the indictment. Seven counts of crimes against humanity under Article 5 of the Statute of the Tribunal. This covers persecutions, persecutions on political, racial and religious grounds committed through a number of acts including killings, cruel and inhumane treatment, unlawful detention, establishment and perpetuation of inhumane living conditions in detention facilities, forcible transfer and deportation, appropriation and plunder of property, wanton destruction of villages and areas and destruction of religious and cultural buildings, imposition and maintenance of restrictive and discriminatory measures, extermination, murder, torture, inhumane acts, deportation and forcible transfer as inhumane acts. These are the crimes against humanity charged in the indictment. Further, six counts of violation of the laws or customs of war, under Article 3 of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we please ask you to slow down for the purposes of the translation? Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: I will certainly do that. I apologise to the interpreter. I will speak more slowly. Six counts of violations of the laws or customs of war, under Article 3 of the Statute of the Tribunal. These are murder, torture, cruel treatment, wanton destruction or devastation of towns or villages not justified by military necessity, and destruction or wilful damage done to institutions dedicated to religion. I will now proceed to give a brief overview of the contents or the facts of the indictment. According to the indictment, Stojan Zupljanin allegedly covered the following positions from 1991 onwards. He was commander of the Regional Security Services Centre, CSB, of Banja Luka, from at least 5 May 1992 until July 1992, he was a member of Autonomous Region of Krajina Crisis Staff and in 1994, he became an adviser for internal affairs to the President of Republika Srpska. It is alleged that between 1st April and 31st December 1992, the RS ministry, the Republika Srpska Ministry of Interior, MUP, forces, acting together with the Bosnian Serb army, VRS, the Territorial Defence and paramilitaries, carried out a campaign to disarm the non-Serb population. The disarmaments campaign was frequently used as a pretext for unlawful attacks on non-Serb villages and their inhabitants. At the same time, it is alleged that the forces under the control of the Bosnian Serb authorities seized power in those municipalities deemed to pose a threat to the accomplishment of the overall plan to create a Serb state within Bosnia and Herzegovina. These takeovers allegedly initialised a series -- initiated a series of events organised and directed by the Bosnian Serb authorities, that by the end of 1992 resulted in the death of thousands and the forced departure of tens of thousands of Bosnian Muslims and Bosnian Croats. The indictment alleges that Stojan Zupljanin, as a commander of the CSB Banja Luka was the most senior police officer in the ARK, subordinated only to the Minister of the Republika Srpska MUP. According to the Prosecution, Stojan Zupljanin had therefore overall authority and responsibility for the functioning of the police within the ARK. It is further alleged that he had operational control over municipal and regional forces in the ARK, including those responsible for the operation of detention facilities. It is further alleged that Stojan Zupljanin exercised command and control of the police at times in coordination with the Bosnian Serb army, paramilitary forces and volunteer units, Territorial Defence and civilian bodies, including regional and municipal Crisis Staffs. In addition to his position as the highest police officer in the ARK, it is alleged that Stojan Zupljanin represented the police on the ARK Crisis Staff. Now, this indictment charges Stojan Zupljanin with individual criminal responsibility under two categories. The first one is based on Article 7(1) of the Statute. You are in fact charged with having committed, planned, instigated, ordered and otherwise aided and abetted in the planning, preparation or execution of the crimes charged. By using the word "committed" the Prosecutor does not allege that the accused physically committed any of the crimes charged. "Committed" in this indictment includes participation in a joint criminal enterprise. According to the indictment, Stojan Zupljanin participated in a joint criminal enterprise, the objective of which was to eliminate and permanently remove by force or other means Bosnian Muslims and Bosnian Croats from the territory of the planned Serb state. The indictment further states that Stojan Zupljanin worked in concert with other members of this joint criminal enterprise, including Radoslav Brdjanin, General Momir Talic, Slobodan Milosevic, General Ratko Mladic, Radovan Karadzic, Nikola Koljevic, Momcilo Krajisnik, Biljana Plavsic, Mico Stanisic and others listed in paragraph 22 of the indictment. Stojan Zupljanin is also charged with criminal responsibility that we refer to as superior command responsibility and this is based on Article 7(3) of the Statute. Basically, what it means is that the indictment alleges that you, while holding a position of superior authority, are also individually criminally responsible for acts or omissions of your subordinates. Before we now proceed to the procedural parts of this initial appearance, the opportunity to enter a plea on the counts of the indictment, I'm going to ask you a few questions. And my first question is, could you please state your full name for the record?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if you permit me, before I give you my full name, about which a lot has been written over the past few days, I would need to clarify some things and I would be very grateful to you for that and I think that would be something that would be of use to everyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: You will certainly be given an opportunity to address the Court, to make a statement. If this has a bearing on the identity issue, you may do it now or we may do it later.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: He's not receiving interpretation. Are you hearing me now?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to discuss this matter now, and I would be very grateful to you if you allow me to do that. It is well known that a number of Serbs accused for war crimes surrendered voluntarily and a number of them was killed or captured by SFOR members and the intelligence services as well as that a group of them was or still is at large. I was one among four who remained at large, Your Honour. Unfortunately, or fortunately, I'm not sure any more, Dr. Radovan Karadzic, General Ratko Mladic and Goran Hadzic are still at large and I wish that they would remain at large forever. When this first group surrendered voluntarily or under pressure, there was a short lull and there was then a lot of media and all other kinds of pressures. We began to be demonised, each one of us was aware that we were about to be shot and life became more and more difficult for us and more uncertain. And then, information reached me that Tadic, Kostunica, Bulatovic, and Vukcevic met, analysed the overall situation and came to the joint conclusion that, I quote, for the Republic of Serbia and Republika Srpska, the best and most useful solution was for the remaining Hague accused at large should be liquidated. So the democratic rulers of Serbia resorted to well-tried Stalinist methods of liquidation. They issued the authorised services with the task to actually carry this out and a secret action for our liquidation was initiated. From that point on, I was exposed to enormous suffering and superhuman efforts to survive. There was a time of fear, hiding and concern. Compared to all of this, prison was a welcome thing. I was afraid of everything and anything, and that lasted for more than four years. And then I was deprived of liberty. Praise God that they didn't know who they were depriving of freedom because I had my original ID documents from the Republic of Serbia and I was thinking about my citizenship and my new name, that a lot has been written about, Branislav Vukadin and there was never an attachment given to the Court in Serbia but to the inspector who was escorting me and this caused confusion for the investigative judge as well. And the only straw to save me was that name and the wish that the media deal with that and that it would come to light what happened and the longer the time passed there were less opportunity for them to take me out of a cell in the middle of the night, to take me in an unknown direction and liquidate me. A lot of lies were written about me dictated by the security and information service in order to destroy my image to the end and to justify their awful act and destroy my family even though they were not aware how many actually they were assisting me because there was no way back from there. In long, sleepless nights in my prison cell sometimes I would wish to be taken to The Hague Tribunal as soon as possible. And this time, finally came, and now here I am, here you are, and as our famous military leader, Karadjordje Petrovic said to the Turks in 1804, the proceedings can begin. As for my remaining brothers that I mentioned, I would like for them to be alive but I'm afraid perhaps night has swallowed them up. I'm really afraid of them and from the bottom of my soul I'm aware of all the suffering and the difficulties they are going through and which I went through myself. I hope that the Lord God helps them and I wish them a long life in freedom. I think it's evident from everything that we have never had any support in Serbia from the current democratic authorities. Quite to the contrary. I'm very unhappy --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Mr. Zupljanin, that was a rather long, rather lengthy answer to my question, if you would be willing to state your full name for the record. I think this suffices for now. You will have, of course, ample opportunities to make submissions to this Tribunal, but I understand from this statement so far that you are then the Zupljanin in the indictment of this -- in this case. Will you be willing to now at this stage to state your full name for the record?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you would just give me one more minute, I would be able to finish everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: If you would, then, keep to the circumstances of your case and not -- we are not in this case and certainly not in this hearing dealing with other fugitives, other indictees of this Tribunal so keep it short and keep it to your own personal things.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. All right. Thank you. I will be very brief. I just wanted to say two more sentences. I'm very unhappy that war broke out at all in the territory of the former Yugoslavia. It is something that I and the long-suffering Serbian people least wanted, but I deeply believe, Your Honour, that I'm going to prove in the course of these proceedings all the untruths from the indictment and that all Serbs, Croats and Muslims will erect a large brilliant monument to me in some square in Banja Luka in order to affirm that war will never break out again and that we would live as brothers just like we did from 1945 to 1990 and that they will never allow anyone to manipulate them again. Since I have not received the indictment I would like to use my right this time not to plead on the indictment even though you wanted to do that, but now I'm going to answer to your question specifically. I state so that there are no more dilemmas on this matter, I am Stojan Zupljanin, the son of Aleksandar and Dragica, born not on the 28th as the Prosecutor mentioned, but actually that's the date of birth of my wife, so I like that date as well, but actually I was born on the 22nd of September, 1991 [as interpreted] in a quiet Bosnian village, Maslovare, in the municipality of Kotor Varos. I am a Serb. I have completed law school and I have passed the bar exam. I am a master of legal sciences since 1995 and, well, whatever you need.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. We can take this in its own order. That would be nice but thank you for that. So the full name is then on the record. And my next question to you is your date of birth. When were you born? Maybe that's already on the record in what you said but your date of birth is 22 September?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was born on the 22nd of September, 1951. My father is Aleksandar and my mother is Dragica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: And you were born in Maslovare?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, in a quiet village of Maslovare, in the municipality of Kotor Varos. It's some 46 kilometres from Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: And then next, if you're willing to state that, also I'll ask for your -- the last address you stayed at, but if you are willing to state that, we will go into private session for that. It's not of interest to the public, that bit. We go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, there is no need to keep this confidential. The public can hear that my last address was in Banja Luka, Stevana Markovica number 3. It's true it's no longer being guarded by the SFOR members as it used to be. Up until now there were always three or four vehicles in front of the building but I think from now on it will still continue to be safe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you. So that's also now on the record. Has your family been informed of your transfer to The Hague and of your detention in the United States detention -- in the United Nations Detention Unit? Or would you like the Tribunal to notify any family member?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm very grateful for the Tribunal for this nice gesture but I have already notified them, or, rather, they learned all about that on Saturday through the media.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you. As for legal representation, as we mentioned already, you are represented here today by duty counsel, and maybe he has had the opportunity to briefly give you some -- give you some guidance as to your rights to counsel, to legal representation. You have a right to be assisted by counsel of your own choosing, subject to certain rules and discretion exercised by the registrar of this Tribunal, or you have the right to represent yourself, if you so choose. The rules also provide for legal aid should you qualify for this according to the rules. Do you have any comments on this? Is it clear for -- is it clear for you, your rights to counsel?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. My rights to counsel are clear to me and I will decide in the forthcoming period what to do. I have already contacted some counsel and I will notify the Tribunal promptly about any decision that I make.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Mr. Zupljanin, I want to ensure that you are informed that you, as an accused in proceedings before this Tribunal, you have certain rights, and these may also have been touched upon by counsel in your brief meeting, as I understood, today, but I want to go a little bit more into your rights. I draw in particular your attention to the rights enshrined in Articles 20 and 21 of the Statute for this Tribunal and among these rights are the following: The right to be informed promptly and in detail in a language you understand of the nature and cause of the charge against you; the right to have adequate time and facilities for the preparation of your defence and to communicate with counsel of your own choosing; the right to be tried in your presence and to defend yourself in person or through legal assistance of your choosing; and as mentioned earlier, the right not to be compelled to testify against yourself or to confess guilt. Do you understand these rights, that you have these rights?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Have you received the indictment in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I have not. But after the hearing, I plan to take receipt of it and I think that I have enough time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: You have a right under the Rules for the indictment to be read out in full. This is a right that you can waive and state for the record that you waive the right for a full reading of the indictment, that for now it is sufficient with the summary that I've given earlier today. Since you already have stated that you're not prepared to enter any plea today, maybe you will waive the right to have a full reading of the indictment? If not, we will read the indictment in full.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since you have been so kind and have given me so much time to tell you what I wanted to say, I don't think that there is any need for us to waste time on that. I will read it, perhaps not only once but several times, and I will avail myself of the right to enter my plea 30 days after today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: And I understand that so far you have had only limited time to go through this at all with counsel present here today. Thank you. And since you already have stated, and it is on the record, that you will not enter a plea, and also referred to the Rules that seemed to suggest to me that you also are aware of the rule of your right to then enter a plea within 30 days from this initial appearance so that is what you will do, you will take the time and revert to this within the 30 day limit, according to the Rules? If you please will state, because the nodding doesn't go into the transcript. If would you state it for the record.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. Yes, I fully agree with you and I think that it is the best time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you. After this initial appearance is adjourned, you will remain in custody for the time being, according to the order that exists for that. You have, however, a right to file an application for provisional release pursuant to Rule 65 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the Tribunal. If you -- I should also inform you that if such a request is filed, you will have the opportunity to avail yourself of legal counsel also for that purpose. For the Prosecution, I would like to remind the Prosecutor that pursuant to Rule 66(A)(i) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the Tribunal, within 30 days of the initial appearance of the accused, will make available to the Defence all the supporting material which accompanied the indictment when confirmation was sought. I'm sure this is something that the Prosecution will act upon.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We are aware of our obligation according to Rules. However, we found it more efficient now to wait until the permanent counsel is assigned because the material can get lost or -- so I think it will -- let's wait until the permanent counsel is assigned. Of course, if he is not assigned within this time period, we will disclose it according to Rules.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you for that. And for the information of the accused, after that, after you have been served with the supporting material, pursuant to Rule 62(A) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the Tribunal, you will have then a 30-day period for filing of preliminary motions, once you have received all this material. And this 30-day time-limit shall not run until the -- until permanent counsel has been assigned to the accused. Is there any matter now that the Prosecution wishes to raise at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. There are no other matters to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you. Any matters to be raised by the Defence at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. We've covered everything that we've planned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you. And it is my duty under the Rules, Mr. Zupljanin, to enquire if you have been treated well in the UN Detention Unit, if you have received adequate health care or assistance. If need be we will go into private session for that but -- do you have any comments to make on the conditions in the Detention Unit?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you allow me before that, just to say one thing, I would like to receive the materials in the Serbian language. I don't speak other languages. I'm familiar with Russian but it's not an official language at the Tribunal so I would like to ask to receive the materials exclusively in Serbian so that I would be able to use them. This is my only request. As for the conditions, if a person can be satisfied with conditions in detention, then I am satisfied and I have no particular remarks to make in that respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: As for the materials in Serbian language, I will not make any comments on that at the moment. Does is the Prosecution have any comment to make on that specific issue?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Of course, the material will be disclosed in the language which the accused can understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: As mentioned we will then arrange for a subsequent hearing within the 30 days from today, for the opportunity -- where the opportunity will be given for the accused for entering a plea. And if by that time you should choose not to enter any plea, even after having consulted with your counsel and having had time to go through the indictment in full and plea -- a plea of not guilty will be entered on your behalf by myself or by the Tribunal. You understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes. I think I have then covered the matters that I wanted to raise today. And if no one has additional comments or matters, we will adjourn this hearing. This hearing is then adjourned.
